  the sums are finite, since~$f$ and~$g$ have compact support. Since these functions are invariant under the action of~$\mathbb{T}_L$, the kernels~$F(p(x), p(y)) = \phi(x - y)$ and~$G(p(x), p(y)) = \gamma(x - y)$ are well-defined on~$\mathbb{T}_L$. Moreover,
  \[
    F(x,x) + G(x,x) = \phi(0) + \gamma(0) = \sum_{v \in L\mathbb{Z}^n} f(v) + g(v) = f(0) + g(0),
  \]
  since~$\operatorname{supp} f \cup \operatorname{supp} g \subseteq [-L/2, L/2)^n$. So, take~$t = L^n f(0) + L^n g(0)$. Since we can take~$L \geq 1$, it follows that~$F(x, x) + G(x, x) \leq t$.

  It is left to prove that~$(t, F, G)$ satisfies the edge and cone constraints of~$\vartheta^*(G_L, \mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{T}_L)_{\mathrm{c}})$. Recall that~$G_L = (\mathbb{T}_L, E)$ with~$xy \in E$ if and only if~$d_L(x, y) \geq 1$. If~$d_L(x, y) \geq 1$, then for every~$v \in L\mathbb{Z}^n$,~$\|x - y + v\|\geq 1$. Hence,
  \[
    F(x,y) + G(x,y) = \sum_{v \in L\mathbb{Z}^n} f(x - y + v) + g(x - y + v) \leq 0.
  \]

  That~$F \in \mathrm{PSD}(\mathbb{T}_L)$ and~$G \in \mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{T}_L)$ follows from the following. Let~$\mu_L$ be the Haar measure on~$\mathbb{T}_L$, normalized so that~$\mu_L(\mathbb{T}_L) = L^n$. Take a function~$\rho \in L^2(\mathbb{T}_L)$, and denote the inner product on~$L^2(\mathbb{T}_L)$ by~$\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{\mathbb{T}_L}$ and the cross-correlation on~$\mathbb{T}_L$ by~$\mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}$.
  Then, by Equation~\eqref{eqn:quotient-measure-is-invariant-Radon-measure}, Lemma~\ref{lem:approximate-by-restrictions}, and because~$(\rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}\hspace{-1.5pt} \rho) \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\circ$}} p$ is continuous, bounded, and periodic,
  \[
    \begin{split}
      \langle F, \rho \otimes \rho\rangle_{\mathbb{T}_L} &= \langle \phi, \rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}\hspace{-1.5pt} \rho\rangle_{\mathbb{T}_L} = \langle f, (\rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}\hspace{-1.5pt} \rho)\mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\circ$}} p \rangle\\
      &=\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^n} \langle f (\1_{C_T} \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} \1_{C_T}), (\rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}\hspace{-1.5pt} \rho)\mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\circ$}} p \rangle\\
      &=\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{n}} \int_{C_T^n}\int_{C_T^n} f(x-y) (\rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}}_{\mathbb{T}_L}\hspace{-1.5pt} \rho)(p(x-y))\, dydx\\
      &=\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{n}} \int_{C_T^n} \int_{C_T^n} f(x-y)\\
      &\phantom{= \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{n}} \int_{C_T^n}}\int_{\mathbb{T}_L} \rho(p(x)+z) \rho(p(y)+z)\, d
      \mu_L(z)dydx\\
      &= \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{n}} \int_{\mathbb{T}_L}\\
      &\phantom{= \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T^{n}}}\int_{C_T^n} \int_{C_T^n} f(x-y) \rho(p(x)+z) \rho(p(y)+z)\, d
      \mu_L(z)dydx\\
      &\geq 0.
  \end{split}\]
  Thus,~$F \in \mathrm{PSD}(\mathbb{T}_L)$, and similarly~$\langle G, \rho \otimes \rho\rangle_{\mathbb{T}_L} \geq 0$ for all~$\rho \in L^2(\mathbb{T}_L)_{\geq 0}$, hence,~$G \in \mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{T}_L)$.

  Finally, since~$F$ is invariant under the torus, to show that~$F - J \in \mathrm{PSD}(\mathbb{T}_L)$ it suffices that the Fourier coefficient of~$\phi$ at~$0$ as a function on~$\mathbb{T}_L$ is at least~$1$. Indeed, since~$f$ has compact support, again by Equation~\eqref{eqn:quotient-measure-is-invariant-Radon-measure},
  \[
    \begin{split}
      \int_{\mathbb{T}_L} \phi(x) \, d\mu_L(p(x)) &= \int_{\mathbb{T}_L} \sum_{v \in L\mathbb{Z}^n} f(x+v)\, d\mu_L(p(x)) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\, dx = \widehat{f}(0) = 1.
  \end{split}\]
  This concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:sp-theta-smaller-than-torus-theta}
  Let~$n \geq 2$ be an integer and~$K \in \mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$. If~$\mathcal{C}(K) \subseteq C_{\mathrm{sym}}(K)$ is a convex cone and~$\mathcal{C} \subseteq C_0(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is a convex cone containing~$\mathrm{K}_K^* \mathcal{C}(K)$, then
  \[
    \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathcal{C}) \leq \frac{\vartheta^*(G_{K}, \mathcal{C}(K))}{\lambda(K)}.
  \]
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
If~$\vartheta^*(G_K, \mathcal{C}(K))$ is infeasible, the conclusion follows. So, let~$(t, F, G)$ be a feasible solution to~$\vartheta^*(G_K, \mathcal{C}(K))$, and let~$f = \mathrm{K}_{K}^* F$ and~$g = \mathrm{K}_{K}^* G$. Then,~$f$ and~$g$ are in~$C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)$. Indeed, the support of both functions is contained in~$K+K$. Since~$\mathrm{K}_K^* = \mathrm{Av}_{\mathbb{R}^n} \mathrm{Res}_K^*$, a straightforward calculation shows that, since~$F$ and~$G$ are uniformly continuous,~$f$ and~$g$ are continuous.

  If~$\|x\| \geq 1$, then
  \[
    f(x) + g(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \bigl(\mathrm{Res}_K^*F(y,x+y) + \mathrm{Res}_K^*G(y,x+y)\bigr)\, dy \leq 0.
  \]
  That~$\mathrm{K}_K^* G \in \mathcal{C}(K)$ follows from the assumption on~$\mathcal{C}$.

  Since~$F \in \mathrm{PSD}(K)_{\mathrm{c}}$, for all finite~$U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the matrix~$\mathrm{Res}_U \mathrm{Res}_K^*F$ is positive semidefinite. Since~$\mathrm{K}_K^* = \mathrm{Av}_{\mathbb{R}^n} \mathrm{Res}_K^*$, it follows that
  \[
    \sum_{u, v\in U} f(u-v) x_u x_v = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \sum_{u, v \in U + z} \mathrm{Res}_K^*F(u, v) x_{u - z} x_{v - z}\, dz \geq 0
  \]
  for all finite~$U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ and~$x \in \mathbb{R}^U$. By~\cite[Proposition 3.35]{Folland2016AAnalysis}, it follows that~$f \in \mathrm{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

  Moreover, since~$F - J \in \mathrm{PSD}(K)$,
  \[
    0 \leq \langle F - J, J\rangle = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} F(y, x+y)\, dydx - \lambda(K)^2 = \widehat{f}(0) - \lambda(K)^2,
  \]
  so that~$\widehat{f}(0) \geq \lambda(K)^2$. Finally,
  \[
    f(0) + g(0) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} F(z,z) + G(z,z)\, dz \leq t \lambda(K),
  \]
  so that~$(f(0) + g(0)) / \widehat{f}(0) \leq t / \lambda(K)$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- theorem-37: body_md -->
\label{thm:smooth-cop-sp-theta-is-exact}
  For all integers~$n \geq 2$,~$\Delta_n = \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}})$.
<!-- end theorem-37 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
The inequality~$\vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}) \geq \Delta_n$ follows from the inequality~\eqref{eqn:SP-theta-under-inclusion} and Theorem~\ref{thm:C0-theta-is-upper-bound}.

  For the other inequality, the strategy is to use Theorem~\ref{thm:cop-theta-exact-packing-graphs} and the expression~\eqref{eqn:sphere-packing-density-limit-over-cubes}, which says that
  \[
    \Delta_n = \lim_{L \to \infty} \frac{\alpha(G_{C_L})}{L^n} =  \lim_{L \to \infty} \frac{\vartheta^*(G_{C_L}, \mathrm{COP}(C_L)_{\mathrm{c}})}{L^n}.
  \]

  By Theorem~\ref{thm:Polyas-theorem-for-invariant-cones} and~\ref{thm:polar-identities},~$\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}} = \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_{A \in \mathcal{B}_{\mathrm{fin}}}\mathrm{K}_A^* \mathrm{COP}(A)$, thus it satisfies the conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:sp-theta-smaller-than-torus-theta}, and
  \[
    \vartheta^{C_0(\mathbb{R}^n)}_{\mathrm{SP}}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}) \leq \vartheta^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}_{\mathrm{SP}}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}) \leq \frac{\vartheta^*(G_{C_L}, \mathrm{COP}(C_L)_{\mathrm{c}})}{L^n}
  \]
  for all~$L$. Taking the limit over~$L$ shows that~$\Delta_n = \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}})$.

  It remains to show that every feasible solution~$(f, g)$ of~$\vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ can be approximated in a suitable way by smooth feasible solutions. To achieve this, make use of Leibniz's rule for differentiation under the integral: if~$\rho$ is smooth and~$\psi$ continuous with compact support, then for all~$i$,
  \[
    (\partial/\partial x_i) (\rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} \psi) = \rho \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} ((\partial / \partial x_i)\psi) = -\psi*((\partial / \partial x_i)\rho),
  \]
  whence the cross-correlation of a smooth function with a compactly supported continuous function is smooth.

  Thus, take a smooth approximate identity~$(\phi_i')_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ where each~$\phi_i'$ has support in~$B_{1/(2i)}(0)$ for~$i \geq 2$. For example, the bump functions defined by
  \[
    \phi_i'(x) =
    \begin{cases}
      N_i \exp^{-1/(1 - 2i\|x\|^2)} &\text{if } \|x\|< 1/(2i),\\
      0 & \text{otherwise,}
    \end{cases}
  \]
  with~$N_i$ a suitable normalization constant, satisfy the requirements. Then, the functions~$\phi_i = \phi_i' \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} \phi_i'$ form a smooth approximate identity where every~$\phi_i$ is supported in~$B_{1/i}(0)$.

  Recall that if~$r \in \mathbb{R}$ and~$\rho : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, then~$\rho_r(x) = \rho(rx)$. Note that~$f_r \in \mathrm{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and~$g_r \in \mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}$ for all~$r \in \mathbb{R}$. Let~$r_i = 1/(1-1/i)$. Then, by Lemma~\ref{lem:action-of-pt-approximate-identity} the function~$r_i^n \phi_i \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} f_{r_i}$ is in~$\mathrm{P}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and~$r_i^n \phi_i \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} g_{r_i}$ is in~$\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}$. Moreover, all these functions are smooth with compact support, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:approximate-by-correlation} they are nonpositive on~$x$ such that~$\|x\|\geq 1$, converge uniformly to~$f$ and~$g$ respectively, and~$\int r_i^n \phi_i \mathbin{\scalebox{.85}{$\star$}} f_{r_i}(x)\, dx = \int f(x)\, dx$ for all~$i$. This shows the theorem.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:cop-sp-theta-exact}
  Let~$n \geq 2$ be an integer. If~$X$ is a vector space such that~$C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n) \subseteq X \subseteq C_0(\mathbb{R}^n)\cap L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, then~$\Delta_n = \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^X(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}})$. In particular,~$\Delta_n = \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\mathrm{COP}(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}})$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
This follows immediately from Theorem~\ref{thm:C0-theta-is-upper-bound}, Theorem~\ref{thm:smooth-cop-sp-theta-is-exact}, and Equation~\eqref{eqn:SP-theta-under-inclusion}.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- theorem-38: body_md -->
\label{thm:convergence-copositive-hierarchy-SP}
  If~$n \geq 2$ is an integer, then
  \[
    \Delta_n = \lim_{r \to \infty} \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_0(\mathbb{R}^n) \cap L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\breve{C}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}) = \lim_{r \to \infty}\vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\breve{C}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}).
  \]
<!-- end theorem-38 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Convergence of the copositive hierarchy for compact packing graphs, Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence-copositive-hierarchy-packing-graphs}, says that
  \[
    \Delta_n = \lim_{L \to \infty} \lim_{r \to \infty} \frac{\vartheta^*(G_{C_L}, C_r(C_L)_{\mathrm{c}})}{L^n}.
  \]
  By Lemma~\ref{lem:local-definition-bC} and Theorem~\ref{thm:polar-identities}, the inclusions~$\breve{C}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}} \supseteq \mathrm{K}_K^*C_r(K)$ hold for all~$K \in \mathcal{K}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, hence by Lemma~\ref{lem:sp-theta-smaller-than-torus-theta}, for all~$L$,
  \[
    \vartheta_{\mathrm{SP}}^{C_c(\mathbb{R}^n)}(\breve{C}_r(\mathbb{R}^n)_{\mathrm{inv}}) \leq \frac{\vartheta^*(G_{C_L}, C_r(C_L)_{\mathrm{c}})}{L^n}.
  \]
  First taking the limit over~$r$ and then over~$L$ concludes the proof.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:continuity-dual-topologies}
  Let~$(X_1, Y_1)$ and~$(X_2, Y_2)$ be dual pairs of vector spaces with respective dualities~$\langle \cdot\, , \cdot\rangle_1$ and~$\langle \cdot\, , \cdot\rangle_2$. Let~$A : X_1 \to X_2$ be a linear map.

  If~$A$ is continuous under a dual topology on~$X_1$ and any topology on~$X_2$ such that~$\langle \cdot\, , y\rangle_2$ is continuous for all~$y \in Y_2$, then~$A'(Y_2) \subseteq Y_1$.

  If~$A'(Y_2) \subseteq Y_1$,~$X_1$ and~$Y_2$ are equipped with dual topologies, and~$X_2$ and~$Y_1$ are equipped with weak topologies, then both~$A$ and the map~$A^* : Y_2 \to Y_1$ given by~$A^*(y) = A'(y)$ are continuous.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Let~$A$ be continuous with respect to an $(X_1,Y_1)$-dual topology on~$X_1$ and any topology on~$X_2$. Suppose that for all~$y \in Y_1$, the functionals~$\langle \cdot, y\rangle_2$ are continuous, and fix~$y \in Y_2$. Then, the functional~$x \mapsto \langle A(x), y\rangle_2$ is continuous. The definition of~$A'$ and the identification~$Y_1 = X_1^*$ together warrant~$\langle A(x), y\rangle_2 = \langle x, A'(y)\rangle_1$, and~$A'(y) \in Y_1$.

  If~$A'(Y_2) \subseteq Y_1 = X_1^*$, the functional~$x \mapsto \langle A(x), y\rangle_2 = \langle x, A'(y)\rangle_1$ is continuous for all~$y \in Y_2$. So, if~$(x_i)_{i \in I}$ is a converging net in~$X_1$, then~$(A(x_i))_{i \in I}$ converges weakly in~$X_2$, and~$A$ is continuous under a dual topology on~$X_1$ and the weak topology on~$X_2$.

  Continuity of~$A^*: Y_2 \to Y_1$ follows by applying the previous argument to~${A'}'$ restricted to~$Y_2$, and~${A'}' = A$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- theorem-39: body_md -->
\label{thm:polar-identities}
  Let~$(X_1, Y_1)$ and~$(X_2, Y_2)$ be dual pairs of vector spaces, each of~$X_1$,~$X_2$,~$Y_1$, and~$Y_2$ with dual topologies. Let~$A: X_1 \to X_2$ be a continuous linear map with continuous adjoint~$A^*$, let~$S_X \subseteq X_1$, let~$S_Y \subseteq Y_1$, and let~$\{S_i\}_{i \in I}$ be an arbitrary family of subsets of~$X_1$. Then:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item[(i)] $(S_X^*)^* = \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} S_X$;
    \item[(ii)] $(A S_X)^* = {A^*}^{-1} S_X^*$;
    \item[(iii)] $({A^*}^{-1} \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} S_Y)^* = \operatorname{cl} A S_Y^*$;
    \item[(iv)] $\bigl(\bigcap_{i \in I} S_i^*\bigr)^* = \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_{i \in I} S_i$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-39 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
\textup{(i)} This follows from~$S_X^* = (\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} S_X)^*$ and~\cite[Proposition 5.5, Example 5.9]{Simon2011Convexity}, since~$\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} S_X$ is convex and contains~$0$.

  \textup{(ii)} Denote by~$\langle \cdot\, , \cdot \rangle_i$ be the duality between~$X_i$ and~$Y_i$. Let~$s \in S_X$ and~$y \in Y_2$. From~$\langle As, y\rangle_2 = \langle s, A^* y\rangle_1$ it follows immediately that~$\langle As, y\rangle_2 \geq 0$ if and only if~$A^*y \in S_X^*$. So~$(AS_X)^* = {A^*}^{-1}S_X^*$.

  \textup{(iii)} Since~$A$ is linear and~$S_Y^*$ is a convex cone,~$AS_Y^* = \operatorname{cone} AS_Y^*$. Then, by~\textup{(i)} and~\textup{(ii)}:
  \[
    \operatorname{cl} AS_Y^* = \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} AS_Y^* = ((AS_Y^*)^*)^* = ({A^*}^{-1}(S_Y^*)^*)^* = ({A^*}^{-1}\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} S_Y)^*.
  \]

  \textup{(iv)} The inclusion~$\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i \subseteq \bigl(\bigcap_i S_i^*\bigr)^*$ holds if~$\bigcup_i S_i \subseteq \bigl(\bigcap_i S^*_i\bigr)^*$ holds. Indeed, each~$S_i^*$ is a closed convex cone, and an intersection of closed convex cones is again a closed convex cone. Then, apply~$\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}}$ to both sides.

  Let~$j \in I$,~$s \in S_j$, and~$y \in \bigcap_i S^*_i$ In particular,~$y \in S_j^*$, so~$\langle s, y\rangle_1 \geq 0$. Thus,~$\bigcup_i S_i \subseteq \bigl(\bigcap_i S_i^* \bigr)^*$ and~$\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i \subseteq \bigl( \bigcap_i S_i^*\bigr)^*$.

  Suppose that~$y \in Y_1 \setminus S_j^*$ for some~$j \in I$. By the definition of the dual there exists an~$s \in S_j$ such that~$\langle s, y\rangle_1 < 0$. But~$S_j$ is contained in~$\operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i$, so~$y$ is not in~$\bigl( \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i\bigr)^*$. Then,~$\bigl( \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i \bigr)^* \subseteq \bigcap_i S_i^*$. By taking the dual again and applying~\textup{(i)}, it follows that~$\bigl(\bigcap_i S_i \bigr)^* = \operatorname{\overline{\mathrm{cone}}} \bigcup_i S_i$.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
